overview: Single-arm feasibility study of peer support in one early intervention in psychosis service during 2027, with progression criteria and embedded interviews.
population: Young people aged 14 to 35 on the caseload who are within three years of a first episode and not in inpatient care at the time of the offer; under-18s with parental consent and their own assent.
exposure: Offer of one-to-one peer support from one of two trained peer support workers, contact in community settings or by text, with fortnightly lived-experience supervision and a written role description including confidentiality rules.
procedures: Care coordinators offer peer support to eligible young people in a fixed order from January 2027. Uptake, contacts and disengagement are recorded in the routine record. The shortest recovery questionnaire is asked in person at baseline and six months by a named worker. Peer workers complete a monthly wellbeing check. Interviews with about 15 young people, 8 family members and 8 staff take place between months 6 and 10.

outcomes.name: Uptake of peer support
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible young people offered peer support who have at least two contacts
outcomes.timing: Within three months of the offer
outcomes.why: The first condition for any trial.

outcomes.name: Retention at six months
outcomes.measure: Proportion still in contact with the service at six months
outcomes.why: Engagement is the outcome a later trial would target.

outcomes.name: Delivery and questionnaire completion
outcomes.measure: Contacts per week delivered; proportion completing the recovery questionnaire at six months
outcomes.why: Shows whether the role and measurement work.

outcomes.name: Peer worker wellbeing and turnover
outcomes.measure: Monthly wellbeing check and any resignation or sickness absence
outcomes.why: The role must not harm the peer workers.

feasibility: Two peer workers at 0.6 whole-time equivalent can support about 40 young people at a time; routine data and one short questionnaire keep the burden low.
biasMitigation: Offer made in a fixed order to avoid clinicians choosing who is offered
Questionnaire asked in person by a named worker
Progression criteria fixed before the first offer
Interviews by a researcher outside the clinical team

biasFlags.label: Selective offering
biasFlags.note: Coordinators may favour engaged young people; the fixed order limits this.

biasFlags.label: Single service
biasFlags.note: Results may not transfer to other teams.

flags: Feasibility, process and balancing measures only; no effectiveness claims
parsimony.simplestPath: One offer, routine records, one short questionnaire and pre-set progression criteria.

theoreticalFramework: Normalisation process theory guides the interviews about how the role is taken up by the team; it earns its place because the question includes whether the role can be embedded.
summary: Feasibility study with uptake as the primary outcome and progression criteria for a trial.
